concerns.concern: The optical 'erasure' has not been distinguished from photo-thermal annealing. A transient temperature rise from the LED, which sits 1 cm above the sample and causes heating jumps, could anneal the trapped state and mimic erasure.
concerns.quote: A transient local temperature rise during illumination would anneal the trapped configuration and mimic "erasure".

concerns.concern: The dielectric measurement probes the whole 0.5 mm substrate. The oxygen vacancies created by Al reduction lie near the surface, so a bulk-averaged loss peak is not obviously an interfacial oxygen-vacancy signature.
concerns.quote: The OVs created by Al reduction are confined near the surface, so a bulk-averaged loss peak is not obviously an interfacial-OV signature.

concerns.concern: The Arrhenius parameters of the dielectric peaks imply relaxation times far from the ~10³ s, nearly temperature-independent dark relaxation seen in transport. The claimed mechanistic link therefore lacks a reconciling model.
concerns.quote: That is not the behaviour of a process gated by barriers of 76 or 236 meV. The authors need a model that reconciles these timescales

concerns.concern: Tc is anticorrelated with mobility in both the gating and illumination protocols. A simple Tc–mobility (or disorder/confinement) relation could explain both observations without invoking polar nanoregions; a Tc vs μ, n, Rs plot for all states is requested.
concerns.quote: A Tc–μ (or confinement/disorder) relation would explain both observations without invoking PNRs.

concerns.concern: There is no direct evidence of remnant polarization. Suggested measurements are C–V/P–V hysteresis, displacement charge, thermally stimulated depolarization current, or SHG.
concerns.quote: There is no direct evidence of remnant polarization.

concerns.concern: Dielectric Peak 2 sits on a rising background and could be an extrinsic Maxwell–Wagner, depletion-layer or leakage relaxation rather than oxygen-vacancy ionization. Bare-substrate controls, leakage vs T and equivalent-circuit fits are requested.
concerns.quote: It could be a Maxwell–Wagner or depletion-layer relaxation, or thermally activated substrate/AlOx leakage, rather than OV ionization.

concerns.concern: Dielectric Peak 1 resembles known impurity-dipole relaxations in KTO, such as Li⁺ off-centre hopping. The substrate's impurity content is not reported.
concerns.quote: The 76 meV peak resembles known relaxations of impurity dipoles in KTO, such as Li⁺ off-centre hopping

concerns.concern: There is an internal inconsistency in the optical mechanism. The paper argues that red light activates the low-barrier processes even at very low temperatures, yet illumination shows no obvious effect at 2 K.
concerns.quote: If the process were photonic, it should operate at 2 K.

concerns.concern: The photon-energy, power and dose dependence of the erasure is untested. Sub-threshold IR illumination in particular is needed to separate defect photo-ionization from heating.
concerns.quote: Measure wavelength dependence, including sub-threshold IR, where heating persists but defect photo-ionization should not.

concerns.concern: The work appears to rely on a single device, and the number of samples and cooldowns is not stated. Key results should be reproduced on at least one more sample, with device-to-device spread shown.
concerns.quote: The manuscript appears to rely on a single device. The number of samples and cooldowns is not stated.

concerns.concern: 'Complete erasure' of the Tc enhancement is not shown. Illuminated transitions are never compared with the pristine pre-gating Tc or Rs, and partial illumination gives graded values.
concerns.quote: Either show full recovery or soften "complete" in the title, abstract and conclusions.

concerns.concern: The text claims τ has minima at 35 K and 95 K, but in Fig. 4c the minima are near 25–30 K and 85–90 K, and 95 K is the global maximum of τ.
concerns.quote: 95 K is the global maximum of τ (~1.38 × 10³ s).

concerns.concern: The ΔR/R₁ maxima at 35 K and 95 K each rest on a single temperature point. Those curves look qualitatively different and noisier than their neighbours, and there seem to be duplicate labels.
concerns.quote: The ΔR/R₁ maxima (Fig. 4b) each rest on a single temperature point.

concerns.concern: SI Fig. 5a appears to follow the same protocol as Fig. 4 but shows no anomalous relaxation at 35 K or 95 K. This suggests a dataset inconsistency, and the authors should clarify whether they are the same data.
concerns.quote: SI Fig. 5a, apparently the same protocol ... shows no anomalous relaxation at 35 K or 95 K.

concerns.concern: The authors should estimate the remnant polarization needed to shift the carrier density by the observed amount and assess whether polar nanoregions in KTO can supply it.
concerns.quote: Estimate the remnant polarization needed to shift n by the observed amount (~10¹²–10¹³ cm⁻²) and assess whether PNRs in KTO can supply it.

concerns.concern: The linear scaling of hysteresis loop size with permittivity is expected for any trapping mechanism, since induced charge scales with ε. It therefore does not identify oxygen vacancies.
concerns.quote: For any trapping mechanism, the charge induced by a fixed V_g scales with ε, so ΔL ∝ ε is expected and does not identify OVs.

concerns.concern: KTO's permittivity is strongly field-dependent, so the zero-bias ε is not the relevant response under ±50 V gating. C(V_g) should be measured and the loop size plotted against induced charge.
concerns.quote: Zero-bias ε measured with a 5 V ac excitation is therefore not the response during the gate loop.

concerns.concern: The photon dose is not controlled across temperature and the optical power is uncalibrated. Temperature trends in relaxation amplitude and τ may partly reflect varying dose.
concerns.quote: Temperature trends may therefore partly reflect the varying photon dose.

concerns.concern: The Tc shifts are only tens of mK against ~0.2 K-wide transitions. A control is needed showing that repeated 10 K ↔ sub-K cooldowns without illumination leave Tc unchanged.
concerns.quote: repeated cooldowns without illumination must leave Tc unchanged.

concerns.concern: The fitted τ is comparable to the ~2 × 10³ s observation window, so single-exponential fits are poorly constrained. Fits should be shown and stretched exponentials considered.
concerns.quote: τ is comparable to the ~2 × 10³ s observation window, so single-exponential fits are poorly constrained.

concerns.concern: Carrier density is higher at −50 V than at +50 V, the opposite of the expected depletion for a negative back gate. The sign convention must be stated.
concerns.quote: For a back gate with the 2DEG grounded, negative V_g should deplete electrons. Please state the sign convention.

concerns.concern: The Hall-measured density change over ±50 V is about twice the electrostatic estimate from the gate capacitance, and this is unexplained.
concerns.quote: The Hall Δn over ±50 V (~4 × 10¹² cm⁻²) is about twice the electrostatic estimate

concerns.concern: Gate cycling increases n from the virgin state but decreases n (with a sharp drop beyond −17 V) from the illuminated state. The proposed mechanism needs to account for both trends.
concerns.quote: From the illuminated state, cycling decreases n, with a sharp drop beyond −17 V (Fig. 2g). The proposed picture needs to account for both.

concerns.concern: KTO(111) 2DEGs are multiband, but n is extracted from a single field. R_xy(B) linearity or two-band fits are needed, and the three separate runs should reproduce the same Rs trajectory.
concerns.quote: KTO(111) 2DEGs are multiband, and n is extracted from a single field (±6 T).

concerns.concern: The −10 nA gate current spike exceeds the capacitive current by orders of magnitude, and the sweep rate is not stated. Transferred charge should be integrated and leakage separated from displacement current.
concerns.quote: The −10 nA spike in SI Fig. 3a exceeds the purely capacitive current C·dV/dt (≈ 17 pA at 0.1 V/s) by orders of magnitude.

concerns.concern: The reported low-temperature permittivity (~1500–2000) is below typical KTO literature values. The authors should address fringe fields, nonlinearity from the 5 V ac amplitude, or a depletion layer.
concerns.quote: The reported low-T ε (~1500–2000) is below typical literature values for KTO.

concerns.concern: Methods describes the LED as current-driven yet says the same voltage was used despite a temperature-dependent I–V characteristic, and the photon flux is not calibrated.
concerns.quote: Methods states that the I_L–V_L characteristic is temperature dependent, with "the same V_L" used although the LED is described as current-driven.

concerns.concern: The gate-current data were recorded after full illumination but are used to explain drift from the virgin state. The virgin first-cycle gate current should be shown.
concerns.quote: SI Fig. 3 was recorded after full illumination, while the main text uses it to explain the drift from the virgin state (Fig. 1).

concerns.concern: The claim that hysteresis arises because PNR/oxygen-vacancy dynamics lag the sweep has not been tested via sweep-rate dependence of the loop size.
concerns.quote: Measure ΔL versus sweep rate at a few temperatures. This would directly test the claim

concerns.concern: A comparison sample with different capping, a different orientation, or a non-superconducting KTO 2DEG would substantially strengthen the mechanism.
concerns.quote: A comparison sample would substantially strengthen the mechanism.

concerns.concern: Because ε(T) is monotonic, plotting against ε is equivalent to plotting against T. The apparent onset and deviation points should be tested against fit-range choices.
concerns.quote: The apparent "onset" and "deviation" points should be tested against fit-range choices.

concerns.concern: It is not established whether parallel conduction or photoconduction occurs in AlOx, bulk KTO or the contacts under illumination. This matters because the whole sample including wire bonds is illuminated.
concerns.quote: Establish whether parallel conduction or photoconduction occurs in AlOx, in bulk KTO or at the contacts under illumination.

concerns.concern: Sample characterization is insufficient. AlOx thickness and stoichiometry, reduction depth (e.g., XPS Ta⁴⁺/Ta⁵⁺) and the oxygen-vacancy depth profile are not reported.
concerns.quote: Report the AlOx thickness and stoichiometry.

concerns.concern: Novelty is overstated relative to prior work on gate-cycling Tc enhancement, trapping-induced hysteresis, persistent photoconductivity and light-induced reset. 'Previously unrecognized' should be toned down.
concerns.quote: The manuscript should state clearly which elements are new, and tone down "previously unrecognized".

concerns.concern: The 'non-volatile' and 'neuromorphic' framing lacks retention data for the gate-imprinted state at base temperature and endurance beyond ~8 cycles.
concerns.quote: please report retention of the gate-imprinted state at base temperature (hours to days) and endurance beyond the ~8 cycles shown.

concerns.concern: The number of distinguishable intermediate Tc states, under dose-controlled erasure and amplitude-controlled writing, is not shown.
concerns.quote: Show the number of distinguishable intermediate Tc states

concerns.concern: Device claims should acknowledge that erasure is performed at 10 K and requires warming out of the superconducting state.
concerns.quote: Erasure is performed at 10 K and requires warming out of the superconducting state. The device claims should acknowledge this.

concerns.concern: The 'similar temperature dependence' of loop size and permittivity in Fig. 3a depends on the arbitrary relative scaling of the two y-axes.
concerns.quote: The "similar temperature dependence" in Fig. 3a depends on the arbitrary relative scaling of the two y-axes.

concerns.concern: Relaxation amplitudes are normalized inconsistently, by ΔR₀ in SI Fig. 5 and by R₁ in Fig. 4.
concerns.quote: Note that SI Fig. 5 uses ΔR₀ while Fig. 4 uses R₁.

concerns.concern: It is not stated whether the lock-in phase reference was calibrated with a known capacitor, which matters because the loss tangent is sensitive to instrumental phase offsets.
concerns.quote: tanδ ≈ π/2 − θ is sensitive to instrumental phase offsets.

concerns.concern: Uncertainties are missing for the activation energies, Arrhenius prefactors, Tc, and the fitted τ and ΔR.
concerns.quote: Please quote uncertainties on E_a1 and E_a2, the ω₀ values, Tc, and the fitted τ and ΔR.

concerns.concern: Some data points in Fig. 3c appear to lie below ln(0.1 Hz), inconsistent with the stated 0.1–4001 Hz frequency range.
concerns.quote: some data points appear to lie below ln(0.1 Hz) ≈ −2.3, which would be inconsistent with the stated 0.1–4001 Hz range.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 3a caption says permittivity curves above 1 Hz overlap, though low-T differences are visible. The Fig. 3 caption also calls 35 K a boundary of significant TO softening although ε rises continuously.
concerns.quote: The Fig. 3a caption states that ε curves for f > 1 Hz overlap, but low-T differences are visible.

concerns.concern: The text says the hysteresis loop is discernible up to ~100 K, but Fig. 3a shows finite loop size up to 180 K.
concerns.quote: the loop is discernible up to ~100 K, whereas Fig. 3a shows finite ΔL up to 180 K.

concerns.concern: In SI Note 4 the 856 Ω value is mislabelled as R_s^b instead of R_s^a, and SI Fig. 5 is captioned 'Extended Figure 5'.
concerns.quote: the 856 Ω post-gating value is labelled R_s^b; it should be R_s^a.

concerns.concern: The van der Pauw/FEM correction factor and its uncertainty are not stated in Methods.
concerns.quote: please state the van der Pauw/FEM correction factor and its uncertainty.

concerns.concern: Editorial issues: units are used inconsistently, a sentence in the Discussion is duplicated, and there are multiple typos.
concerns.quote: Units are used inconsistently (Ω vs Ω·sq⁻¹; Fig. 2c labels). There is a duplicated sentence in the first paragraph of the Discussion.
